# Casa — Home Assistant app

Canonical current-state documentation for AI agents working on this repository.
Code is the source of truth; these files are a map.

## Architecture

- [architecture/agent-taxonomy.md](architecture/agent-taxonomy.md): How an agent is declared, validated and looked up — tiers, required artifacts, and the registry.
- [architecture/configuration.md](architecture/configuration.md): Where configuration comes from, what is version-controlled, what reload can pick up without a restart, and how secrets resolve.
- [architecture/engagements.md](architecture/engagements.md): Work one agent hands to another — ephemeral delegation, durable engagements, how they end, and what survives a restart.
- [architecture/http-surface.md](architecture/http-surface.md): The two HTTP servers, what each exposes, and how an inbound request is authenticated.
- [architecture/mcp-and-tools.md](architecture/mcp-and-tools.md): How tools reach an agent, and where authorization for a tool call actually happens.
- [architecture/memory.md](architecture/memory.md): Long-term memory — how a fact is written, who may read it back, and what a caller is told when the store cannot answer.
- [architecture/overview.md](architecture/overview.md): What Casa is made of — supervised services, the three agent tiers, and where configuration enters.
- [architecture/personality.md](architecture/personality.md): What an agent is versus how it presents — role artifacts, personas, bindings, and which prompt is actually served.
- [architecture/plugins.md](architecture/plugins.md): How a plugin becomes usable — registry, content-addressed store, artifact identity, and per-call authorization.
- [architecture/telegram.md](architecture/telegram.md): How Telegram messages become turns — transports, authentication, the per-topic causal log, keyboards, and rendering.
- [architecture/triggers.md](architecture/triggers.md): What makes an agent act without a person speaking — scheduled and webhook triggers, and the consent a plugin trigger needs.
- [architecture/turn-loop.md](architecture/turn-loop.md): How one inbound message becomes one agent turn, and what bounds it.
- [architecture/voice.md](architecture/voice.md): How spoken input becomes a turn and how the answer gets back — transports, authentication, the turn budget, and deferred delivery.

## Doctrine

- [doctrine/publishing.md](doctrine/publishing.md): The one rule that decides whether a fact may be written down in this repository.

## Contributing

- [contributing/doc-contract.md](contributing/doc-contract.md): The shape a document takes, and which of its rules CI enforces versus a reviewer.
